description: FIRST MILESTONE (user's stated priority): Electropneumatic + Step-by-step, end to end. From a parsed SequenceModel produce the complete logical circuit: steps, end-of-course sensors, one control relay/memory per step with a topologically-correct SEAL/SELO holding contact, solenoids, the ladder (electrical) logical model, the pneumatic logical model (5/2 double-solenoid main valves + double-acting cylinders), and a textual chronological explanation derived from the SAME model. Includes the CircuitValidator (full check list) and golden + property tests. Depends on FEAT-001.
steps: Implement src/engine/step-by-step: a solver that consumes the SequenceModel and produces a CircuitLogicalModel. Apply the three PMR3407 step-by-step rules exactly: (1) a line energizes only if the previous line is active; (2) only when the previous step's end-of-course sensor is tripped; (3) energizing a line de-energizes the previous line. Model each step's 'subcircuito basico' as a relay Ki with a SEAL contact (its own NO contact in parallel with the activation condition, holding Ki energized), gated by Ki-1 and the previous step's sensor, and reset by a Ki+1 NC contact. Add the EXTRA rung to arm the last line. Handle simultaneous movements (parenthesized group) as one shared line/step, and timer (T) steps as a time-relay gating the transition. Handle cycle mode: single = last line does not re-arm first; continuous = last line re-arms first line.

Implement the electropneumatic naming/mapping in the solver: sensors per cylinder (e.g. 1S1/1S2 for A retracted/advanced per the convention chosen in RULES.md), solenoids 1Y1/1Y2 (advance/retract) etc., relays K1..Kn, boxed-delay time relay for T steps. Map each step's movement(s) to the correct solenoid energization in the ladder power section.

Implement the pneumatic logical model for the same milestone: one double-acting cylinder per actuator, one 5/2 double-pilot (double-solenoid) main directional valve per cylinder with port labels (P=1, A=2, B=4, R=3, S=5, pilots 12/14), driven by the solenoids from the ladder. Keep this as a logical Circuit (components + connections), not SVG.

Implement src/validator/CircuitValidator: detect connection to nonexistent component, connection to nonexistent port, required port unconnected, duplicate component, reference to nonexistent sensor, reference to nonexistent relay, coil without component, impossible transition, step without exit condition, and logical conflicts. Return structured issues; the pipeline must refuse an invalid circuit rather than emit it.

Implement src/simulator (at least the state model + a step-execution scaffold) so the explanation and future simulation share the model: Cylinder states RETRACTED/MOVING_FORWARD/EXTENDED/MOVING_BACKWARD, Relay ON/OFF, Sensor ACTIVE/INACTIVE, Valve STATE_1/STATE_2. Provide a deterministic executor that walks START -> Ki energized -> solenoid -> valve switch -> cylinder moves -> end-of-course sensor -> next step.

Implement the automatic textual explanation generator that derives the chronological narrative (START pressed; K1 energized; K1 energizes Y1; valve of cylinder A switches; A advances; a1/1S2 active; enables next step; ...) FROM the same logical model / simulator trace. Do not maintain a separate parallel logic.

Write tests/golden for at least three worked exercises: (a) electropneumatic step-by-step 'A-B+B-B+B-TA+' (deck 2 Ex4a -> K1..K6 with a time relay on the T step, solenoids 1Y1/1Y2/2Y1/2Y2); (b) step-by-step 'A+B+B-A-' (deck 2 -> K1..K4); (c) at least one more worked step-by-step sequence. For each golden test record input, method, type, and assert the expected logical result: number of steps/relays, per-step sensor and solenoid mapping, presence and correct topology of the seal contact, and the extra arming rung. Where feasible assert structural features (component counts, connection endpoints).

Add a REGRESSION test that specifically fails if the seal/selo contact is misplaced: construct the step-by-step circuit, then assert that step Ki remains energized (relay ON) in the simulator after the cylinder LEAVES the sensor that started step Ki (i.e. the holding path does not depend on the transient sensor). A mutation that removes/misplaces the seal contact must make this test fail.

Write tests/properties (using the hand-rolled arbitrary from FEAT-001) asserting invariants over random valid sequences: every movement maps to some actuator's action; every referenced sensor exists; every connection ends at a valid port; every step is reachable; no step points to a nonexistent step; no identifier exists without a corresponding component; and for sequences ending in the initial state, the model can verify that property. Run the CircuitValidator over generated circuits and assert zero issues.
Run typecheck and the full test suite; ensure all golden, regression, and property tests pass. Record in findings the exact pass counts and any convention decisions the golden tests encode.
acceptance_criteria: For 'A+B+A-B-' the step-by-step solver produces exactly 4 steps mapped to relays K1..K4 with correct per-step solenoid energization and end-of-course sensor gating.
For golden 'A-B+B-B+B-TA+' the solver produces 6 steps K1..K6 with a time relay on the T-prefixed step and solenoids drawn from {1Y1,1Y2,2Y1,2Y2}; the golden test asserts this and passes.
The seal-contact regression test passes with the correct topology and FAILS when the seal contact is removed/misplaced (demonstrating it catches the bug).
CircuitValidator detects every listed error class (unit tests construct a bad circuit for each class and assert the corresponding issue is reported).

The textual explanation is generated from the simulator/logical model (single source of logic) and lists the chronological START -> Ki -> Y -> valve -> cylinder -> sensor -> next-step narrative for a golden sequence.
Cycle mode is honored: continuous re-arms the first line from the last; single does not.
`unset NODE_OPTIONS && tsc --noEmit` and `unset NODE_OPTIONS && node --test ...` both pass with all milestone tests green.
findings:
FIRST MILESTONE complete: electropneumatic step-by-step end to end. tsc --noEmit passes; node --test passes with 53/53 tests (27 pre-existing FEAT-001 + 26 new for FEAT-002). New tests: tests/golden/step-by-step.golden.test.ts (5), tests/golden/seal-regression.test.ts (3), tests/golden/explanation.test.ts (2), tests/engine/validator.test.ts (11), tests/properties/step-by-step.property.test.ts (5).

Architecture (single source of logic): src/engine/model.ts defines CircuitLogicalModel (plan steps + ladder rungs with typed contact ROLES + pneumatic model). src/engine/step-by-step/solver.ts applies the three PMR3407 rules. src/engine/circuit.ts projects the model to a flat domain Circuit for validation/render. src/simulator/{state,simulator,explanation}.ts run the deterministic START->K->Y->valve->cylinder->sensor->next-step cycle and DERIVE the textual explanation from the same trace. src/validator/validator.ts is the CircuitValidator.

Conventions encoded (from docs/PMR3407_RULES.md): 1S1=retracted/1S2=advanced (A2); 1Y1=advance/1Y2=retract; relays K1..Kn one per step; timer step -> timer relay with boxed delaySeconds (default 0.3). Seal (SELO) topology: each control rung has a dedicated seal BRANCH holding the relay's OWN NO contact, in parallel with the activation branch [prev-line NO + prev-sensor NO] (step 0: START + arming contact), reset by the next line's NC contact (rule 3). Extra arming contact on rung 1 driven by the last relay: NC for single cycle, NO for continuous (continuous also adds a wrap reset of the last line from the first).

Seal regression: tests/golden/seal-regression.test.ts simulates that K1 stays ON after START is released (momentary) AND the home sensor 1S1 opens; a mutation removing the seal branch makes K1 drop (test asserts the mutation fails) and the validator flags the seal-less model as VAL_LOGICAL_CONFLICT.

Golden exercises: A+B+A-B- (4 steps), A+B+B-A- (4 steps), A-B+B-B+B-TA+ (6 steps, K6 = timer relay, solenoids from {1Y1,1Y2,2Y1,2Y2}).

Simulator notes/decisions: (1) a solenoid may be driven by multiple power rungs (e.g. both K1 and K3 command A+ via 1Y1) so solenoid coils are computed as the logical OR over their power rungs (naive rung-by-rung last-writer-wins oscillates). (2) Physics applies at most ONE physical event per round then re-settles the ladder, which keeps single-cylinder-reuse sequences (A+A-A+A-) deterministic. (3) initialSimState assumes all cylinders start retracted; sequences that logically begin extended (A-...) are handled at the parser initialState level and asserted structurally in golden tests, not via full simulation (a later feature can thread InitialState into the simulator). Cascade, layout, SVG and the React UI are intentionally NOT implemented (FEAT-003/FEAT-004).

V1 REVIEW REMEDIATION (2026-09): addressed review issues 1, 2, 4, 5 that touch the step-by-step solver/simulator/validator (still status=completed). CHANGES:
- ISSUE 1 (BLOCKING, seal proof vs REAL simulator): exported settleLadder from src/simulator and added a maxPhysicalEvents cap to runCycle. tests/golden/seal-regression.test.ts now proves K1-holds-after-1S1-opens through the PRODUCTION engine (runCycle pulseStart + real settleLadder), not only the local evaluator; the mutation half is retained. A settleLadder regression that dropped the seal now fails a test.
- ISSUE 2 (continuous mode unsimulated) + a real bug it exposed: the OLD continuous arming put a NO K_last contact in SERIES with START on rung 1, so the FIRST press could never start the cycle (K_last is OFF at rest -> continuous produced NO relay activity at all). FIXED in solver.ts: continuous now emits the wrap as a PARALLEL branch ([K_last NO] OR [START]) so the initial press works and the last line re-arms the first. New tests/golden/cycle-mode.simulation.test.ts drives runCycle in both modes: single fires K1 once and stops (completed, K4 latched); continuous re-fires K1 after K4 (wrap) and the first-relay reset drops K4.
- ISSUE 4 (timer delay): kept the documented deferral (grammar has no delay token). Made it explicit in RULES A4 and pinned by tests/engine/timer-delay.test.ts (default 0.3s; caller-supplied defaultDelaySeconds threaded through; non-timer steps carry no delay).
- ISSUE 5 (simultaneous-group gating): added PlanStep.enableSensorIds (all arrival sensors of the predecessor). The activation rung now gates on EVERY member of a simultaneous predecessor in series (AND), not just the last-listed one; validator IMPOSSIBLE_TRANSITION checks all member sensors; STEP_WITHOUT_EXIT considers enableSensorIds. New tests/golden/simultaneous-gating.test.ts: model exposes both member sensors, rung has a contact per member, and real settleLadder holds the next relay OFF until ALL members arrive. RULES A6 documents the no-co-termination-assumed gating.
Test count for this milestone's files: seal-regression 3->4, +cycle-mode 2, +timer-delay 2, +simultaneous-gating 3. Full suite now 99 tests pass (was 87), tsc --noEmit clean.
